history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 387 / 'Shri Baglamukhi Mata Temple' (Bankhandi) - same temple. TOWN CORRECTION: CSV town 'Jwalamukhi' is WRONG - the temple is at Bankhandi in Kangra district (near Jawali/Sameli), on the Delhi-Pathankot highway. This is a prominent Siddha Peeth dedicated to Goddess Baglamukhi, the 8th of the ten Mahavidyas of Tantric Shaktism, revered as Pitambara (clothed in yellow) for stambhan shakti - the power to paralyze enemies, silence speech and grant victory in legal disputes. The temple, entrance, domes and pillars are painted yellow and devotees dress in yellow and offer besan ki laddoo. Legend says Rama, guided by Hanuman, worshipped Baglamukhi here before the battle with Ravana and received the Brahmastra; the Pandavas are said to have built the temple overnight during their exile; and the goddess herself emerged from the Haridra Sarovar ('lake of turmeric') to calm a cosmic storm at Vishnu's request. Tantric sadhana continues at the site during Navratri and Amavasya. One source lists it among the Nava Shaktipeeth Yatra sites (verify). Coordinates below are from the geocoder's 'Maa Bagulamukhi Temple, Jawali' match - APPROXIMATE, precision not verified.

town_description: Bankhandi (also spelled Bakhandi) is a village in Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh, on the Delhi-Pathankot highway near Jawali and Sameli. It sits within the Kangra Valley's famous Shakti belt, close to the Jwalamukhi and Chintpurni shrines. The Mata Baglamukhi Temple makes it a major pilgrimage stop on the Kangra Valley circuit; the surrounding foothills and forests give it a quiet Himalayan setting.
